newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates ease amid good liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates ease amid good liquidity.

text.p: Croatian money market rates took a slight step down in slow trade on Wednesday as all banks enjoyed continued high liquidity.

"All banks were positive so there was no overnight trade on Tuesday," a dealer told Reuters. Banks' accounts rose to 657 million kuna from Tuesday's 635 million, she said, adding that many banks took the initiative to repay their borrowings.
"The banks are searching for ways to find borrowers for their money," she said.
But modest demand for fresh kuna funds froze daily trading by 0820 GMT at seven million kuna, against 130 million on offer.
Two million was call money granted at a steady eight percent and five million were 60-day loans struck at 16 percent, down from Tuesday's 18 percent.
"It's lower because there is so much money in circulation now," the dealer said.
Banks had 25.2 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from Tuesday's 14.2 million, the central bank said. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom +385 1 455 7075
